children: JGBs edge lower in price terms in early Tokyo trade amid higher oil prices that typically cause inflation in Japan and could prompt a faster pace of BOJ rate hikes. The focus for today may shift to Japanese Finance Ministry's auction of about 2.5 trillion yen of 5-year sovereign notes. "We expect the auction to draw a certain degree of demand, clearing smoothly," SMBC Nikko Securities' Lisa Mochizuki says in a research report. With the five-year tenor "having cheapened versus surrounding zones, it's looking more attractive on a" relative value basis, the junior analyst adds. The five-year JGB yield is up 0.5 bps at 2.345%. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
